answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price entry in scarce, verifiable work rather than free signups. Picture a logging cooperative: before an agent may trade timber futures, it must stake compute to attest its identity, like a falcon ringed before hunting rights are granted. Reputation then spreads through the network like a ripple across water, so one operator spawning hundreds of clones gains no extra trust, because each clone inherits only a fraction of stake-weighted reputation and must independently earn attestations from existing peers before its signatures count.
